sources.text:
Bull Island (Irish: Oileán an Bhulla), more properly North Bull Island (An Bulla Thuaidh or Oileán an Tairbh Thuaidh), is an island located in Dublin Bay in Ireland, about 5 km long and 800 m wide, lying roughly parallel to the shore off Clontarf (including Dollymount), Raheny, Kilbarrack, and facing Sutton. The island, with a sandy beach known as Dollymount Strand running its entire length, is a relatively recent, and inadvertent, result of human intervention in the bay. The island lies within the jurisdiction of, and is mostly owned by, Dublin City Council, and is managed by the Council's Parks and Landscape Division.
Bull Island, which is accessed by way of a causeway bridge from Raheny and a wooden bridge from Clontarf, has the most designations of any site in the country, as a National Bird Sanctuary, a biosphere reserve, a National Nature Reserve, a Special Protection Area under the EU Birds Directive, and a Special Area of Conservation under the EU Habitats Directive, while also being the subject of a Special Amenity Area Order.  Most of the island-proper is a car-free zone.  It holds a wide variety of plant and bird species, and a limited range of mammals, one reptile, one amphibian...

stops.name: Bull Island
stops.detail: Bull Island, richtiger North Bull Island, ist eine Insel in Dublin Bay in Irland, etwa 5 km lang und 800 m breit, etwa parallel zum Ufer vor Clontarf, Raheny, Kilbarrack und mit Blick auf Sutton. Die Insel mit einem Sandstrand, der als Dollymount Strand bekannt ist und seine gesamte Länge hat, ist ein relativ neues und unbeabsichtigtes Ergebnis menschlicher Eingriffe in die Bucht. Die Insel liegt in der Gerichtsbarkeit des Stadtrats von Dublin und befindet sich hauptsächlich im Besitz des Stadtrats von Dublin und wird von der Parks and Landscape Division des Rates verwaltet.
